name: Neck curls with plate

lead: Neck curls with a plate are a weighted forward bend of the neck meant to build the muscles at the front and sides of the neck. Forum users do them for a thicker neck and a more masculine overall look, and post progress photos; some also claim jaw and facial changes.

Resistance on neck flexion works the sternocleidomastoid, which bends the neck forward when both sides contract. Material on the exercise comes from forum discussion, and no clinical trial of loaded neck curls for appearance is available.

paras: Users lift or hold a weight plate on the head while bending the neck forward, as part of a lifting routine, with results reported over weeks to months of regular training.
Forum members report multi-day soreness, and one reported dizziness and nausea. No clinical safety data on loaded neck curls for appearance are available.

chain: Front and side neck muscles grow
angle.text: Forum users perform loaded neck curls with a plate to grow the front and side neck muscles for a thicker neck and a more masculine frame, with some also claiming jaw and facial changes. The exercise is popular on forums, with no trials on appearance.

lead: Neck curls with a plate are a form of loaded neck flexion: a person lifts or holds a weight plate on the head while bending the neck forward, aiming to thicken the muscles at the front and sides of the neck. In looksmaxxing forums the exercise is discussed as a way to build a thicker neck and, by extension, a more masculine overall look.

Material on the exercise is limited to forum discussion, which this article cites only for what members say. No clinical trial of loaded neck curls for appearance is available among the sources used here. The muscle chiefly responsible for forward neck flexion, the sternocleidomastoid, is described in general anatomy references [1].
infobox: Thicker neck; sometimes jaw and facial claims

paras: The sternocleidomastoid runs from the breastbone and collarbone to the bone behind the ear, and bends the neck forward when both sides contract together [1]. Loaded neck curls place resistance on this movement, typically by holding a plate against the forehead or head.

Members post before-and-after photos attributed to neck curls and ask how long the person trained [2]. Beginners describe sets of around twenty repetitions as exhausting, and one member reports several days of soreness when turning the head after resuming the exercise [3]. Others ask whether curls enlarge the trapezius as well as the sternocleidomastoid [3].

Several threads ask whether neck curls and chin tucks help the jaw or face, with participants disagreeing about whether they are useful [4]. One poster reported feeling ill, dizzy and nauseated after two sets and asked whether the exercise was responsible; replies suggested acid reflux as a possible cause [5].

lore.intro: Neck curls are discussed in looksmaxxing forums as a facial-adjacent exercise, often grouped with chin tucks [4].
